explanation.1_directionAwarePillarRedefinition: 1.2 replaces the fixed 'centerline - width/2 - width/2' rock pillar by the direction-aware profile-support gap at the closest-centerline pair (gap = d - support_branch(+u) - support_ramp(-u), gravity-aligned D-profile: width/2 sideways, height up, 0 down). Every winnerExcavationSeparations entry therefore changes by construction. Where the closest-pair direction is lateral the value is unchanged; where it has a vertical component the lower drive's full height is charged (stricter); where it has a component along the branch's own axis the cross-section contributes less than a half-span (looser than the old rule). Helix accesses leave the winding outward, so their post-taper samples mostly fall in the last two cases: TABULAR CCW pillars move 10.67-13.53 -> 10.53-15.53 m, WARPED-301 10.12-13.81 -> 10.11-15.67 m, GEOMETRY-STRESS 11.21-22.36 -> 11.67-26.86 m.
explanation.2_tabularWinnerChange: TABULAR-REFERENCE / CUT_AND_FILL feasibleCount 1 -> 2 and winner SPIRAL-n1-CCW-e+0-g0.100 -> SPIRAL-n1-CW-e+0-g0.100. Under the width rule the CW helix had 12/13 accessible levels (min pillar 10.01 m, INFEASIBLE on one level); under the direction-aware gap that level finds a valid branch and the CW candidate (total 3.8157) edges the CCW (3.8441) - the CW was already the lower-scoring geometry, it was only excluded by the pillar reading at one level. The CW winner's per-level pillars are 9.99-15.53 m and plan separations 40.6-53.5 m (CCW: 33.5-50.0 m). HONESTY: the CW minimum pillar 9.987 m at L07 lies 0.013 m below the 10 m floor and is accepted by the PRE-EXISTING commit-B SEPARATION_TOLERANCE of 0.05 m (unchanged in this commit, never widened); it is reported as-is rather than hidden, and tightening that tolerance is a separate decision, not a v2 change.
explanation.3_normalVsExhaustive: Section 1.5 table attached (normalVsExhaustive): TABULAR normal 2 / exhaustive >0 with winnerNormal == winnerExhaustive -> normal; no threshold or proxy was tuned. missedFamilies remains the documented bounded-shortlist limitation (rule 165 audit): the family slot validates each family's best cheap candidate, which can fail the detailed gates while a costlier family member would pass.
explanation.4_unchangedCases: GEOMETRY-STRESS keeps SWITCHBACK-k1-p+20-CCW-g0.100 with identical junctions, access lengths and total score (6.772066); WARPED-301 / IRREGULAR keep SPIRAL-n1-CCW-e+0-g0.120 with two branches re-selected under the new gate values (L10 / L13 plan separation 34.0 / 35.2 -> 44.9 / 45.1 m), totals 4.1428 -> 4.1214 and 5.9501 -> 5.9287 from the shorter access development; WARPED-307 stays NO_FEASIBLE_CANDIDATE (proven geometry); ACCESS-INFEASIBLE stays 0 by design.
explanation.5_certificationConsistency: 1.1 changes no search outcome: the stage-4 policy of every candidate is unchanged; what changes is that selection materialization, the tunnel sweep, the level builder and the development sweep now reuse that policy instead of the whole-body COARSE one (regression: a WARPED fixture whose access branches certify only under the refined bound survives a fresh-process tunnel + development sweep). level_accesses.json additionally carries clearanceBasis (candidate-actual) / clearanceErrorBound / clearanceRefinement.
explanation.6_shortlistFloorAndMessage: 1.3 (shortlist_size >= len(FAMILY_ORDER), schema-validated) and 1.4 (candidate-local basis in the clearance failure detail) have no effect on the default-configured golden outcomes.
